# Kokoro-82M TTS notebook — fleet-sweep fixes

**Source:** the 2026-10-05 static fleet sweep of `main` flagged this notebook for the old restart guard (in-kernel
`pip install` followed by "Restart the runtime" on stale modules) and for a missing guided layer (3 of 9 guided
markers in a notebook that declares `GUIDED`). This is a targeted fix; **no full Notebook Review Framework v1 review
has been done**.
**Base:** `main` at `223df80`.
**Notebook:** `tutorials/kokoro_tts_colab.ipynb`, regenerated by `tools/build_notebook.py` (`build_notebook.py/2.2`).
**Readiness:** **Verification pending.** The fixes are verified offline only; a hosted one-pass Run all is still required.
**Status labels:** unchanged (`STATUS.md`, release status and `clean_runtime_evidence` are left for the maintainer).

Every change is made in the generator, the template, the validator or the lock inputs; the notebook is regenerated and
`--check` is clean. The default path computes the same thing as before (same text, voice, speed, seed, validation,
synthesis, report and exports). What changed on it is how the runtime is installed, the guided layer, and the inline
audio player.

## User-visible changes

- Section 1 is one collapsed infrastructure cell that builds (or reuses) `dimer_isolated_env_<lock digest>/` and routes
  later cells to it; nothing is installed into the kernel and Run all needs no restart. The first run downloads the
  locked PyTorch CUDA stack into that folder, as the in-kernel install did. Linux x86_64 runtimes only.
- New committed files `tutorials/requirements-colab.lock.txt` (113 hashed entries) and
  `tutorials/requirements-colab-extra.in` (the `pip` entry).
- Section 4 gains a `BYOD_PATH` form field; BYOD refusals are named errors instead of a bare `StopIteration`.
- Section 6's inline player is an HTML5 `<audio>` element carrying the written WAV (the isolated environment has no
  IPython); outside a notebook front end the cell prints where the WAV is, as before.
- Guided-layer markdown throughout; the closing gains Troubleshooting, Change one thing, Glossary and Conclusion sections.
- `docs/release-verification.md`: two lines that described the in-kernel install and restart guard now describe the
  isolated bootstrap. No status text changed.

## Verification (offline; not clean-runtime evidence)

- Real input: none of the model stages can run here (the Hugging Face Hub is unreachable and torch is not installed);
  no pretrained-inference evidence is claimed. Checkpoint numbers are quoted from the retained 2026-09-13 run record,
  not produced here.
- Synthetic / stand-in: the Section 1 bootstrap is executed with a stand-in environment (a symlink to the test
  interpreter and a matching lock marker): it reuses the environment without downloading, starts the worker, keeps it
  and its variables on a re-run, routes cells and raises on a worker error. The Section 4 BYOD cell is executed with
  temporary text files and a fake `google.colab.files.upload`. Section 6's player class is executed on a stub WAV.
- `python tools/build_notebook.py --check`: OK. `python tools/validate_release_assets.py`: PASS. `ruff check src tests
  tools`: clean. `pytest` (CI deps: pytest 8.4.2, ruff 0.16.6, numpy 2.5.3, package `--no-deps`): 30 passed before →
  44 passed after.
- `uv pip install --dry-run --require-hashes --only-binary :all: --index-url https://pypi.org/simple -r
  tutorials/requirements-colab.lock.txt` into a `uv venv --managed-python --python 3.12.12`: resolves; nothing installed.
